title: This week
body:
Softmax

- For a 49-key row: 225 ALMs, 0 DSPs and 1 M10K (8192 bits). Measured HPS latency: INT8 5.51 µs; FP32 13.12 µs. Fabric RTL: 606 cycles, projected 8.08 µs at 75 MHz.
- On 10 local images, top-1 / top-5 predictions agreed 100% / 100% with FP32. INT8 relative RMSE: 6.56% on probabilities and 2.60% on attention context. Prediction agreement is not ground-truth accuracy.
- Per-image workload: 4704 rows × 49 scores. HPS INT8: 25.93 ms compute + 2.51 ms estimated bulk transfer = 28.44 ms. Fabric: 38.01 ms projected RTL + 2.01 ms estimated bulk transfer = 40.02 ms.
- Next: validate transfer assumptions and measure integrated board latency under matched conditions before choosing whether to offload.

LayerNorm

- For a 192-channel token: 950 ALMs, 13 DSPs and 6 M10Ks (22016 bits). Measured HPS INT8 latency: 40.43 µs with exact correction or 158.13 µs with integer division; FP32: 7.76 µs. Fabric RTL: 3337 cycles, projected 44.49 µs at 75 MHz.
- On 10 local images, both FP32 and the INT8 replacement achieved 100% top-1 / top-5 accuracy against image labels. LayerNorm output relative RMSE was 3.49%. This is a small local test, not a full-dataset accuracy benchmark.
- Per-image workload: 784 tokens × 192 channels. HPS INT8: 31.70 ms compute + 1.25 ms estimated bulk transfer = 32.95 ms. Fabric: 34.88 ms projected RTL + 0 ms assumed bulk transfer = 34.88 ms.
- Combined with Softmax, estimated totals are 61.39 ms on HPS INT8 and 74.90 ms on fabric. Fabric is 13.51 ms slower under these assumptions; these are operator-workload estimates, not measured full-model inference times.
- Next: validate the 0 ms fabric transfer assumption and measure integrated board latency. Full tables, CSVs and source screenshots: ECE496 Files & Data (https://vit-fpga-wiki.pages.dev/#/files).
